chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: The Cabaliers and records made in Chicago
summary: Welburn asks about the Cabaliers; McRae recalls recording "Minnie the Moocher" and "I'll Be Around" in Chicago.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: The Cabaliers, that's what he called his little band, I think, the Cabaliers.
They were vocals, or was that a small group like a choir or something?
It says here that the Cabaliers and vocals. They recorded in New York December 1924, Christmas Eve -- 1941 right after Pearl Harbor.
No, I don't know who they were, the Cabaliers. That must've been another group he had with him at that time.
Of course, you were in the band at that time. (Inaudible).
"Minnie The Moocher", I did, "I'll Be Around." We recorded "Minnie The -- we recorded that in Chicago.
